beats.trigger: ## From Personal to Team
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: You cannot really share an agent.
beats.got: Sharing an agent is not simple, and what you share is a choice. I don't yet see what it costs.

beats.trigger: A licence rollout, a shared drive, a portal, an internal tool.
beats.got: I'm asked about a licence nobody used. We have one: the BI licences bought two years ago, used by almost nobody. That I can answer.

beats.trigger: **Leave** with one named conversation and one test
beats.got: A list of verbs. None of them has a cost or a payback.

beats.trigger: Pick one teammate who could use what your agent produces.
beats.got: There are four ways to share: context, skill, push and pull. I don't have an agent yet, so I'm picking a teammate for a thing I haven't built.

beats.trigger: Your teammate doesn't want your agent. They want a job done.
beats.got: Start from the colleague's job, not the tool. That's how I'd judge any investment.

beats.trigger: does it name one teammate, their current way of doing the job, and an outcome you could observe?
beats.got: The agent writes up my controller's month-end job and I check it against what I know. An outcome I can observe is something I can use.

beats.trigger: If the reason is merely *"we already have the platform,"* send it back.
beats.got: Don't pick the tool because it's already paid for. I've watched that happen in three programmes.

beats.trigger: You now have the teammate's job and a candidate selected against it.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: Now find the obstacle that decides whether the teammate can actually absorb it
beats.got: The obstacle is the next thing to find.

beats.trigger: A good bottleneck explains why several other obstacles stay hard.
beats.got: Look for the one obstacle behind the others. In my case it's probably IT approval for finance data.

beats.trigger: A polished technical file beside a people file full of unnamed roles is the finding, not a finished rollout.
beats.got: A plan with no named owner is not a plan. That's the risk I'd raise to the board, and here it's named before I raise it.

beats.trigger: checks the assumptions underneath these plans
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: The technical and people plans are hypotheses.
beats.got: The plans are guesses until someone tests them.

beats.trigger: what would have to be true for this teammate, doing this job, to fire their current hire and use my candidate?
beats.got: A good question to ask of any vendor pitch: what has to be true for us to switch? I'd use it in procurement.

beats.trigger: Six months from now, the teammate went back to the incumbent.
beats.got: I write the failure story before it happens. It's like a pre-mortem, which I accept. Still no cost anywhere.

beats.trigger: A candidate picked because it fits the infrastructure is shopping.
beats.got: Pick against the outcome, not the infrastructure. It's a decent rule, though it's a rule and not a number.

beats.trigger: One law decides whether a sharing plan works.
beats.got: A law is coming. I'm waiting to see whether it has evidence.

beats.trigger: The two get reported as one number and they are not one thing.
beats.got: Licences issued is not use, and we report them together. That is exactly how our digital programmes looked fine on paper.

beats.trigger: The proposal got neither a yes nor a no.
beats.got: A good analysis ended without a decision because the people deciding had not done the work. I've sat in that meeting. The story is honest and has no figure, which I would have liked.

beats.trigger: They had not spent any of their own weeks inside it.
beats.got: Deciders need to be inside the work. A delivered report doesn't count.

beats.trigger: The fourth does not copy at all
beats.got: Context, boundary and checks copy. Accountability doesn't. Someone with a name has to answer for it.

beats.trigger: The right choice is the one that fits the week your teammate already has.
beats.got: Each of the four strategies asks something different of the colleague.

beats.trigger: Your candidate is not competing with nothing. It is competing with that.
beats.got: The competitor is the spreadsheet or the colleague they use now. Fair, and the same for any investment.

beats.trigger: Send them a message today and ask for twenty minutes of their week.
beats.got: A small, concrete step I can do. It costs twenty minutes.

beats.trigger: Run this in the same session.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: A role with no name on it tells you who to talk to next.
beats.got: Start from the job, pick one of four, find the bottleneck, name the people, test the switch.

beats.trigger: **Bring what your Monday contact said, in their own words.**
beats.got: Evidence from one real person comes before more building.

beats.trigger: Module 8 puts the agent to work on the building.
beats.got: nothing new

take_homes: Access isn't use. A licence count tells me nothing about whether anyone works differently. I should ask for usage and outcome, not seats.
A plan with a role but no name on it is not a plan. Ask who answers for it.
Before buying or sharing a tool, ask what would have to be true for the person to drop what they use today.

monday.move: Message my controller and ask for twenty minutes on how she writes the month-end variance commentary today. The point is to learn her current method, not to hand her a tool.
monday.when: Monday morning, meeting within the week
monday.stop_condition: If she says the commentary is quick and nobody is waiting on it, I drop it. I won't push a tool onto a job that isn't a problem.
monday.blocker: IT hasn't approved any AI tool for finance data. I'd have to take that to the CEO and IT lead first.

misconception.why: I still think of AI as a licence you buy. But the point that licences issued and people actually changing how they work are different numbers fits my own experience with earlier programmes. I wasn't told what a capability costs or what it pays back, so I'm not fully convinced.

one_line: Sensible and honest about why rollouts stall, and it gave me one small thing to do on Monday. I still didn't get a cost or a payback figure, which is what I came for.
